origin.description: Join a vector with commas, a two-item separator, and a final and.
origin.usage: ansi_collapse(x, sep = ", ", sep2 = sub("^,", "", last), last = ", and ", trunc = Inf, width = Inf, ellipsis = symbol$ellipsis, style = c("both-ends", "head"))

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: Separator when there are more than two items.

arguments.name: sep2
arguments.text: Separator for exactly two items. The default drops a leading comma from last.

arguments.name: trunc
arguments.text: How many items to show. both-ends shows at least five when it truncates.

arguments.name: style
arguments.text: both-ends or head. A unique prefix is accepted.

arguments.name: ellipsis
arguments.text: The mark for omitted items. None uses the current ellipsis symbol.

origin.details: A missing item makes the result missing. An empty vector is an empty string. both-ends with a finite width ignores that width. head with a finite width is not translated.
origin.value: One string, or None when an item is missing.

translation.description: Join a vector with commas, a two-item separator, and a final and.
translation.usage: ansi_collapse(x, sep=", ", sep2=None, last=", and ", trunc=inf, width=inf, ellipsis=None, style="both-ends")

translation.example:
from cli import ansi_collapse
letters = list("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz")
print(ansi_collapse(letters, trunc=5))
print(ansi_collapse(letters, trunc=5, style="head"))
